commandModelNote: Registry model: packages/tui/src/app/slash/registry.ts builds ONE builtin table by spreading 13 per-owner impl arrays (registry.ts:31-63); CommandRegistry indexes byName + byAlias and throws on duplicate names (registry.ts:74-82). Visibility is a HARD gate: visible(ctx)===false means the command is neither listed by completionEntries() nor matched by matches() (registry.ts:101-110), and the loop renders 'Unsupported command: /<name>' for any unmatched slash line before it can become a user prompt (loop.ts:2097-2113). The gate vocabulary is the typed SlashCapability union in types.ts:21-32 (session-create | session-list | dashboard | provider-settings | rewind | compact | fork | context | plan-mode | guardian | vim-mode); the loop derives ctx.capabilities from REAL backend/host members in Loop.slashCapabilities() (loop.ts:2419-2431), which pushes only session-list, session-create, dashboard, rewind, compact, fork, context and provider-settings. plan-mode, guardian and vim-mode are NEVER pushed, so /plan, /view-plan, /auto, /always-approve and /vim-mode are unreachable in the shipped TUI by construction. Two commands bypass the registry table: /settings, /provider and /model are intercepted earlier in the submit path by tryG1SlashModal (loop.ts:2091-2094, 3173-3195), and the registry entries for them are the inventory + forwarding surface (g1.ts:1-10). Commands whose SlashContext member is optional (types.ts:149-199) guard on presence and toast rather than no-op; /rename does NOT guard on BackendClient.rename because that member is unconditional on the embedded client (embedded.ts:814). backendStatus taxonomy used here: implemented = the behaviour exists and is reached on the shipped TUI host path; optional-seam = the behaviour exists but the member it drives is an optional BackendClient/SlashContext member that an assembly may omit, in which case the command resolves to a toast (or a silent no-op where noted); stub-toast = the run body is only a toast or a hard gate that is never satisfied by slashCapabilities(), so no backend behaviour is wired; unsupported = no behaviour at all. Every evidence line below was opened; verified=true means the cited lines were read in this audit.

commands.summary: Turns the always-approve permission stance on.
commands.mechanism: Registered in approval.ts:23-31 with visible() = hasCapability(ctx,'guardian') (approval.ts:27); the gate is a hard gate in CommandRegistry.matches (registry.ts:107). run() calls applyStance(ctx,true) (approval.ts:14-21), which guards on the optional SlashContext.setAlwaysApprove member and otherwise toasts 'always-approve: live guardian capability not wired'. The loop wires setAlwaysApprove to setAlwaysApproveStance (loop.ts:2513), which calls the host seam opts.setAlwaysApprove and flips app.mode/prompt.alwaysApprove (loop.ts:3159-3167). Because slashCapabilities() (loop.ts:2419-2431) never pushes 'guardian', the command is never visible nor matched in the shipped TUI.
commands.gate: capability:guardian (SlashCapability, types.ts:31) — never supplied by Loop.slashCapabilities(), so effectively unreachable

commands.summary: Second name for the always-approve stance toggle (same flip as /always-approve).
commands.mechanism: Registered in approval.ts:32-39 gated on the same 'guardian' capability (approval.ts:35) and routed through the identical applyStance helper as /always-approve (approval.ts:36-38 -> approval.ts:14-21). Note that both commands pass on=true: /auto never turns the stance back off, the flip is Shift+Tab or the settings modal. Same unreachable gate as /always-approve: 'guardian' is never in Loop.slashCapabilities() (loop.ts:2419-2431).

commands.summary: Interjects a side question into the running turn without replacing the prompt.
commands.mechanism: Registered ungated in run.ts:84-96. With an argument the run calls ctx.toggleBtwWith(question) (run.ts:91), wired in the loop to toggleBtwWith (loop.ts:2461): it writes app.paneData.btw {question,state:'asking'} and calls backend.steer(question) (loop.ts:2803-2818), i.e. the question rides the live queue as an interject rather than a new submit. With no argument it calls ctx.openBtwInput() (run.ts:94), which opens the bindTextInput overlay (loop.ts:2832-2839, text-input.ts:23-55); an empty submitted line toasts 'btw cancelled'.

commands.summary: Compacts the conversation immediately (shadow + summary).
commands.mechanism: Registered in run.ts:25-42, visible() = hasCapability(ctx,'compact') (run.ts:29). run() first guards on the OPTIONAL BackendClient.compact member and toasts 'compact: backend seam absent (session-compact not wired)' when it is missing (run.ts:31-34) — the optional-member honesty the design doc flags. When present it awaits backend.compact(arg) and toasts 'compacted' or 'compacted: nothing to compact' (run.ts:36-37), toasting 'compact failed: …' on rejection (run.ts:39). The embedded client implements compact unconditionally (embedded.ts:822-826) via assembly.compactNow (the M33 session-executor surface); 'compact' is pushed by slashCapabilities() whenever backend.compact !== undefined (loop.ts:2426).
commands.gate: capability:compact (types.ts:27), derived in loop.ts:2426 from backend.compact !== undefined

With a numeric argument it validates /^\d+$/ (toasting 'jump: expected a turn number (1..N) or no arg' otherwise, navigation.ts:32-35), indexes ctx.jumpAnchors() and calls ctx.gotoLine(anchor.line), toasting 'jump: turn N out of range' for an index past the end (navigation.ts:36-41). Without an argument it opens the 'jump' panel whose onSelect also calls gotoLine (navigation.ts:44-50). gotoLine sets app.scroll = {offset, follow:false} (loop.ts:2449-2452); jumpAnchors comes from the engine's user-block turn walk (loop.ts:2448).

commands.summary: Renames the session title (with a prompt overlay when no argument is given).
commands.mechanism: Registered ungated in sessions.ts:87-105. With an argument run() calls ctx.renameSession(title) directly (sessions.ts:94); without one it opens a bindTextInput overlay prefilled with app.title whose submit calls renameSession (sessions.ts:98-103), and cancel toasts 'rename cancelled'. The loop wires renameSession to Loop.renameSession (loop.ts:2494, implemented at loop.ts:2990-3006): it trims to 200 chars, toasts 'rename: empty title' for an empty value, updates app.title/app.prompt.title, then calls backend.rename — and because BackendClient.rename is UNCONDITIONAL on the embedded client it persists; a backend without the member falls back to the honest toast 'rename: backend seam absent — title updated in-session only' (loop.ts:2999-3005). The embedded rename appends a session/title event through applyTitle so the title flows back on the event stream (embedded.ts:814-817).

commands.summary: Cycles the theme, or sets it directly by name.
commands.mechanism: Registered ungated in visual.ts:44-59. A bare /theme advances through THEME_ORDER (system → grok-night → grok-day → tokyo-night → rose-pine-moon → oscura-midnight → system) via nextTheme and calls ctx.setTheme(next) (visual.ts:34-41, :50); a named argument is canonicalized ('auto' → 'system') and must be in THEME_ORDER or the command toasts 'theme: unknown … (system | grok-night | …)' (visual.ts:51-57). ctx.setTheme is wired to themeCommit (loop.ts:2479-2483), the shared preview/commit/rollback path that persists the choice; a persist failure toasts 'theme: not persisted — <message>'.
commands.backendModule: Loop.themeCommit (packages/tui/src/app/loop.ts:2479, implemented at :2864) over the settings store (SettingsTheme, packages/settings)

commands.summary: Toggles the turn-timeline rail in the scrollback's right columns.
commands.mechanism: Registered ungated in timeline.ts:10-19; run() negates app.showTimeline and writes it directly on the app state (timeline.ts:15-17) with an on/off toast. The rail is additionally gated at DRAW time by views/timeline.ts: showTimeline must be true AND the pane width ≥ 60 AND turns ≥ 2 (views/timeline.ts:45-53) — so a successful toggle can still produce no visible rail. The host seeds the initial value from opts.showTimeline (default OFF, loop.ts:196-199, :594).

The toast reports the new value because it is computed after the write (visual.ts:66). No backend call.

commands.summary: Writes the transcript to a temp file and opens it in $PAGER.
commands.mechanism: Registered ungated in tools.ts:52-59; run() awaits ctx.openTranscriptPager() and toasts 'transcript: pager opened' or 'transcript failed' (tools.ts:56-57), wired to Loop.openTranscriptPager (loop.ts:2500, implemented at loop.ts:3113-3139). That writes the serialized display rows to `<tmpdir>/ih-transcript-<ts>.ansi`, then spawns $PAGER on it (shell:true) when PAGER is set; on Windows without PAGER it falls back to `cmd /c start <file>` and otherwise spawns `less` (loop.ts:3121-3134).

commands.summary: Runs, lists and inspects workflow jobs (run <name> | status [id] | list).
commands.mechanism: Registered in workflow2.ts:131-177 with the 'workflows' alias (workflow2.ts:134). run() resolves ctx.workflow and toasts 'workflow: surface not wired' if absent (workflow2.ts:138-141); 'run <name>' validates the name against surf.list() BEFORE prompting for params (unknown name → 'workflow run: unknown workflow "<name>"', workflow2.ts:152-161), then opens a text-input overlay whose whitespace-separated key=value tokens become the params map (workflow2.ts:34-43, :113-126) and calls surf.run, toasting the job id and refreshing the status panel; 'status [id]' opens the status panel with [r] refresh and row-select stop (workflow2.ts:65-85, :87-105); bare /workflow or 'list' opens the registry index (workflow2.ts:169-172); anything else toasts the usage line (workflow2.ts:174). The loop supplies the surface through workflowSurface(), which caches opts.workflow or builds createDefaultWorkflowSurface(workspace) (loop.ts:2517, :2612-2615). The default surface uses @i-harness/workflow's registry scan of <workspace>/workflow/*.yml plus the executor over a local node:child_process exec shim with its own job map (workflow2.ts:279-307, :227-274).

cliNotes: apps/cli/src contains only index.ts, run.ts, web.ts, sessions.ts and provider-runtime.ts; there is no acp.ts/sdk.ts/tui.ts. runSdkCommand and runAcpCommand are inline in apps/cli/src/index.ts (declared at :410 and :580), and the tui flag parser is apps/tui/src/index.ts:438 (the package @i-harness/tui-app, imported at apps/cli/src/index.ts:29).

The bin entry is apps/cli/package.json:71-74, declaring both 'i-harness' and 'ih' -> ./bin/i-harness.js; that shim re-spawns node with the tsx loader plus apps/cli/src/index.ts and forwards process.argv.slice(2), propagating the child's exit code (apps/cli/bin/i-harness.js:27, :31).

NO parser supports the --flag=value form: every parser compares whole tokens (apps/cli/src/index.ts:50-56 and :94-300 and :410-620; apps/cli/src/sessions.ts:45-65; apps/tui/src/index.ts:438-467). So --port=5000, --sandbox=read-only and --mode=minimal are all unrecognized — silently ignored outside `run`, and swallowed into the task text inside `run`.

Usage-string versus parser mismatches, recorded as-is: the top-level tui usage line (apps/cli/src/index.ts:36) omits --session-dir and --mode although parseFlags accepts both; the tui's own usage string (apps/tui/src/index.ts:460-461) omits --mode, --fullscreen and --session-dir; the sessions usage string documents --json only for list although the parser and runSessionsCommand accept it for show as well (apps/cli/src/sessions.ts:52, :192-195).

web diverges from run/sdk/acp on --session-dir: run/sdk/acp fail loud on a missing value ('--session-dir requires a directory', apps/cli/src/index.ts:231, :417, :587) whereas web silently falls back to the default store root (apps/cli/src/index.ts:113 with apps/cli/src/web.ts:406).

The M62 web sandbox fix is settings-based, not flag-based: the web branch reads no --sandbox flag; the mode is opts.sandbox ?? settings.get().sandboxMode after settings.load() (apps/cli/src/web.ts:469-470), so passing 'web --sandbox ...' is a silent no-op.
--sandbox must follow the `run` token: 'i-harness --sandbox read-only run task' has args[0] === '--sandbox' and therefore launches the TUI (apps/cli/src/index.ts:164-168).

Flags parsed but with no effect: tui --yes sets flags.yes, which is never read (apps/tui/src/index.ts:102, :439, :445 are its only occurrences); acp --no-auto-approve is a pure presence test so '--no-auto-approve=false' does NOT disable auto-approve (apps/cli/src/index.ts:610).

Environment fallbacks that shadow flags: PORT (apps/cli/src/index.ts:109; apps/cli/src/web.ts:95-99), I_HARNESS_TOKEN / I_HARNESS_HMAC (apps/cli/src/index.ts:105-106), I_HARNESS_TELEMETRY=1 (apps/cli/src/index.ts:205); the tui additionally reads GROK_MOUSE_REPORTING_TOGGLE (apps/tui/src/index.ts:656), I_HARNESS_DIST (:489) and the harness home.

The CLI was NOT executed for this audit; every CLI statement above is read from the cited source lines, and the load-bearing ones (--yes no-op, SIGINT 130 / SIGTERM 143, run --sandbox fail-loud, web storeRoot fallback, --port silent fallback, sessions show exit 2, bin entries) were re-opened and confirmed during the audit.
